40 airlines have now signed on to use Starlink for in-flight Wi-Fi.

Not 40 that are testing it.

~ 5 fully installed and operational
~ 11 actively rolling out
~ 24 announced or in testing

When we wrote about 37 airlines a few weeks ago, it was already the fastest adoption in aviation history.

It is now 40.

The chart tells the story. Every other in-flight Wi-Fi provider is flat. Starlink is vertical.

The in-flight internet market did not gradually shift toward Starlink.

It collapsed into it.

SpaceX just revealed the AI1 satellite.

This is not an internet satellite.

This is a data center in orbit.

~ 70-meter wingspan
~ 20-meter deployed height
~ 150 kW solar array
~ 150 kW peak compute payload
~ 110 m² deployable liquid radiators to manage heat in space

SpaceX built the rocket. Then the internet. Then the global network. Now the orbital computer.

Launch provider. Satellite operator. Global internet. Orbital compute.

That is the progression. And it is not done.

The Moon Mass Driver
Asked what comes after the TeraFab, Elon Musk gave the most surprising answer of the interview.

A mass driver on the Moon.

The logic:

~ A terawatt is still small. To go three more orders of magnitude requires lunar manufacturing.
~ Build solar panels, radiators and potentially chips directly on the Moon.
~ The Moon has no atmosphere and one-sixth Earth's gravity.
~ That means you can launch AI satellites into deep space using an electromagnetic rail gun. No rocket needed.

This is essentially a linear electric motor that throws satellites into space at low cost.

The Mars mission is already underway.

The Moon is the staging ground for everything that comes after.

Video

The TeraFab Scale
To reach a terawatt of AI compute output per year, SpaceX needs a chip factory at a scale that does not exist.

That is the TeraFab.

Elon Musk on the size:

~ 100 million square feet of factory floor
~ 10x larger than the entire Tesla Gigafactory Texas
~ Designed to produce one billion full-reticle chip equivalents per year
~ Each chip producing roughly one kilowatt of compute

For context, current global AI chip manufacturing tops out at around 100 gigawatts per year of total compute.

The TeraFab is built for 1000 gigawatts.

That is 10 times the current global capacity, from a single facility.

Latency From Space
The biggest misconception about space-based data centers is latency.

People imagine signals taking forever to reach Earth.

Elon Musk on the math:

AI satellites orbit 600 to 800 kilometers above Earth.
Light travels 300 kilometers per millisecond.
That puts the satellite roughly 3 milliseconds away.
For comparison, a typical home internet connection has 15 to 30 milliseconds of latency just within your own city.

Space is closer to you than your nearest neighborhood data center.
